messages:
eli: alert: apiserver WATCH latency spikes + controller-manager leader flips in us-east-1a. GPU job queue is growing, throughput ~30% down. anyone oncall?

maya: on it — pulling apiserver and kube-proxy logs now

ops-bot: ALERT: apiserver.high_watch_latency us-east-1a 1749234567

jamal: seeing a lot of 502/connection reset from kube-proxy -> apiserver. kernel logs show MSS/fragmentation errors. possible MTU/path issue after last overlay push

maya: curl from control-plane to 127.0.0.1:6443 ok. from node: `curl -vk https://apiserver.internal:6443` times out, TLS handshake stalls

eli: etcd leader looks stable but fd/io spikes during the watch storm. `etcdctl endpoint status` doesn't show unhealthy but compaction backlog is increasing

sre-lead: thoughts: protect apiserver with lower inflight and consider increasing controller-manager leader-elect timeouts so flips don't cascade

maya: dumping apiserver metrics -> `apiserver_request_latencies_microseconds{verb="WATCH"}` 95th ~= 18s currently

jamal: i can repro with `ping -M do -s 1400 apiserver.internal` -> packet too big / fragmentation. path MTU observed ~1380. We pushed overlay MTU 1400 to GPU subnet two days ago

ryan: that matches a hypothesis: large watch responses (full pod lists with annotations) get fragmented -> fragments dropped -> retransmit -> huge latency for WATCH. controllers keep retrying -> leader election churn

eli: short-term mitigations: reduce apiserver `--max-requests-inflight` and `--max-mutating-requests-inflight`, or break large object payloads (not quick). Another quick option: stabilize kube-proxy by switching mode or restarting to clear conntrack entries

maya: proposed plan (two-step): 1) revert MTU change on non-gpu subnets (rollback network change) 2) canary restart kube-proxy on a few nodes in us-east-1a to clear conntrack. roll gradually. any objections?

jamal: :thumbsup: will canary restart on 3 nodes now and watch metrics

k8s-bot: NOTICE: controller-manager leader elected: controller-manager-1 -> controller-manager-2 (flap count: 4)

ops-bot: note: GPU pod pending count up 120 in us-east-1a, this will increase reserved capacity spend if not drained

sre-lead: temporary policy: throttle GPU pod admission for low-priority workloads. jamal, can you open a quick admission webhook to pause priority < 500 until this stabilizes?

jamal: opening a short-lived webhook now, will point it at ops sandbox.

maya: canary kube-proxy restart command used:
```
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy -n kube-system --selector=topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-east-1a 
```
using `--max-unavailable=1` for safety

maya: canary result: watch latencies dropped from ~18s 95th to ~600ms after the three-node restart. controller-manager stopped flipping leaders

eli: good. rolling through remaining nodes now with same conservative pace. GPU pending count also dropping as scheduler sees apiserver healthy

eli: logs snippet during the storm:
```
Apr 21 12:03:12 kube-proxy[1234]: conntrack: table full, dropping packet from 10.2.0.45:54432 -> 10.0.1.12:6443
Apr 21 12:03:13 kernel: IPv4: packet too big, mtu=1380 next hop=10.0.0.1
Apr 21 12:03:14 apiserver[5678]: watch handler error: EOF
```

maya: immediate follow-ups: revert overlay MTU change for GPU subnets, schedule proper validation for MTU change windows, add regression alert for WATCH latency and controller-manager leader flip count

sre-lead: postmortem items: 1) network change validation gap 2) no automated watch-latency alert 3) don't change MTU on production clusters without staged probe of large watch payloads. Assigning owners

eli: filing incident ticket and adding remediation steps. also propose adding a short runbook: "apiserver-watch-high -> check path MTU + conntrack + kube-proxy restart canary"

maya: thanks everyone. i'll finish the rollout and update the incident once overlay MTU is reverted

ops-bot: REMINDER: open support case with network provider for the overlay MTU regression and ask for trace logs of fragment drops

eli: closing thread from oncall POV — system stable, latency back to baseline. will follow up in postmortem doc.
